confidence_note: The old text's sweeping statistics (doubled obesity, Alzheimer's 'exploded') and 'low cholesterol strongly correlates with decline' are the author's claims or unverified and are dropped or hedged. Kept: US government dietary goals in 1977 urged less fat; Perlmutter argues the shift to carbohydrate-rich low-fat food harmed the brain; he says the brain is rich in fat; some researchers call Alzheimer's 'type 3 diabetes'. These are the author's views and are contested; mainstream guidance still advises limiting saturated fat.
facts: In 1977 the US government published dietary goals that told Americans to eat less fat.
Food makers responded with low-fat products, and low-fat labels filled the shelves.
Perlmutter argues that when fat came out, refined carbohydrates and sugar went in.
He says the brain is largely made of fat and that cholesterol is a building block of brain cells.
He argues the real threat is the repeated rise in blood sugar from refined carbohydrates, linked to insulin resistance.
He mentions that some researchers call Alzheimer's 'type 3 diabetes'.
These claims are the author's argument and are disputed; many health bodies still recommend limiting saturated fat.
tension: A guideline meant to protect hearts may have pushed people toward sugar, in the author's view.
opening_idea: Start in 1977 with the government telling people to eat less fat, and the shelves filling with low-fat food.

lessons.idea: Check what replaces something you remove, because the replacement can matter as much as the cut.
lessons.anchor: Fat removed from food, refined carbohydrates added.

reflect_final: Think of one thing you cut from your diet or routine: what quietly took its place, and is that replacement better for you?

use_cases.situation: You buy a 'light' version of a snack.
use_cases.move: Read the label and compare sugar in the light and regular version before choosing.

use_cases.situation: A relative praises a low-fat diet.
use_cases.move: Say 'Perlmutter argues the swap from fat to carbs backfired; I am not sure, want to read about it?'

use_cases.situation: A colleague is planning team lunches.
use_cases.move: Suggest one option without added sugar and see who picks it.

pocket_idea: When you remove something from your plate, check what replaced it.

conversation_variants.punchline_idea: The 1977 order to eat less fat put low-fat labels on every shelf, and Perlmutter says sugar filled the gap.
conversation_variants.thirty_sec_idea: In 1977 US dietary goals told people to eat less fat, and food makers launched low-fat products. Neurologist David Perlmutter argues refined carbohydrates replaced the fat and that this harms the brain. His claims are disputed.
